description: Figure 3, located at the top of the page, displays two sets of pie charts illustrating the problem distribution based on correctness under the "w/ knowledge" and "w/o knowledge" settings, using the CoT (Chain-of-Thought) and Verify-All methods. The top row of charts, labeled "CoT," shows the distribution for easy, medium, and hard problems. For easy problems, the CoT method with knowledge (N+K+) resulted in 40.6% correct answers, while without knowledge (N+K-) it was 45.9%. For medium problems, the results were 44.6% (N+K+) and 44.3% (N+K-). For hard problems, the results were 36.2% (N+K+) and 36.8% (N+K-). The bottom row of charts, labeled "Verify-All," shows the distribution for the same problem difficulty levels. For easy problems, the Verify-All method with knowledge (N+K+) resulted in 61.5% correct answers, while without knowledge (N+K-) it was 34.6%. For medium problems, the results were 65.4% (N+K+) and 30.8% (N+K-). For hard problems, the results were 39.6% (N+K+) and 30.6% (N+K-). The legend indicates that N+K+ corresponds to the green color, N-K+ to yellow, N-K- to orange, and N+K- to red. The percentages for each category are clearly labeled within the corresponding slices of the pie charts.
